signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + BoJ Tightening Repricing
signals.text: The G10 currency strength scorecard registers an extreme leader-laggard gap of 3.371% over the one-week window. JPY leads the G10 complex with a 1W average gain of +1.821% across 7 pairs, while SEK anchors the laggard board at -1.550% across 2 pairs. BoJ holds at 1.0%. JPY continues its systemic bid despite running a negative carry deficit against the G10 board, reflecting acute rate-hike repricing. Trade bias: Bullish JPY/SEK, theme outperformance driven by policy repricing. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — rate hike decision. Risk: BoJ holds rate at 1.0% and defers the hike, precipitating a fast unwind of the weekly JPY gain.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Positioning Squeeze + Vol Skew + BoJ Repricing
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 153.59, holding well below its daily SMA20 at 157.91, SMA50 at 159.85, and SMA200 at 158.42. The pair faces severe asymmetric squeeze conditions as CFTC Leveraged Funds sit heavily short JPY at -111,297 contracts (2nd percentile, z -2.18), with net short exposure surging WoW by -29,678 contracts. Options markets show intense demand for downside protection, with 1M 25d risk reversals at -2.09 reflecting extreme put skew while 1M IV at 9.5% trades below HV30 at 10.1% for a -0.6% vol risk premium. BoJ holds at 1.0%. Retail positioning is trapped long at 86%, further compounding capitulation downside risk. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, crowded spec short covering dominates carry advantage. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — rate hike decision. Risk: BoJ leaves policy rate unchanged at 1.0%, prompting an aggressive bounce back toward the 157.91 SMA20.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Spec Long vs Retail Sentiment Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7173, testing the immediate resistance of its SMA20 at 0.7164 while holding above the SMA50 at 0.7065 and SMA200 at 0.7001. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold an extended net long position of +50,250 contracts, sitting in the 94th percentile of its 52-week historical distribution with a z-score of +1.79. In contrast, retail positioning from Myfxbook displays an extreme 91% short skew, setting up an acute institutional versus retail divergence at a key technical boundary. While the RBA at 4.35% maintains a -71bp OIS carry advantage over the Fed at 3.75%, leveraged fund net length stalled WoW with a 3,328-contract trim, signaling late-trend momentum exhaustion. Trade bias: Neutral/range AUD/USD; stretched institutional length caps upside near current levels. Catalyst: Fed meeting 16 Sep — policy rate decision. Risk: Sustained daily close above 0.7200 triggers retail short capitulation and forces another trend extension.
evidence: RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75% — 71bp OIS AUD carry advantage

signals.title: EUR/USD — Transatlantic Inflation Divergence + Policy Spread
signals.text: EUR/USD trades flat at 1.1613, compressed directly beneath its daily SMA20 at 1.1629 and SMA200 at 1.1637 while holding above the SMA50 at 1.1529. Headline US August CPI printed at 0.4% month-on-month against a 0.0% consensus, lifting year-on-year CPI to 3.4% and putting upward pressure on front-end US rates where the 2Y yield pushed to 4.43%. ECB holds at 2.5%. The 25-delta risk reversal sits neutral at -0.11 with 1M IV at 5.1% versus HV30 at 4.0%, indicating an options market that is comfortable hedging near-term range-bound conditions rather than pricing a directional breakout. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, policy yield differential and upside US inflation surprise constrain spot upside. Catalyst: Fed meeting 16 Sep — policy rate decision. Risk: Dovish Fed rhetoric or a decisive break above the 1.1637 SMA200 resistance cluster.
